title: Toolchain integration smoke corpus and regression plan (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft of a compact 'smoke + edge' corpus and regression plan for onboarding new model revisions into our tool-use / function-calling stack. The goal: provide a small, high-signal test suite that catches regressions in (1) tool selection, (2) argument parsing/serialization, and (3) multi-step orchestration across tool chains. This is intentionally lightweight so infra can run it on every candidate build as a fast pre-commit or pre-release gate.

Background / Motivation:
- Full eval suites are slow and expensive. We need a small fast suite that still correlates with user-facing failures.
- Past regressions that shipped: silent argument truncation (AM-2987), tool-selection flip when model update changed prompt-balancing (AM-3310), and context bleed in multi-step flows (AM-3591).
- This doc proposes concrete prompt templates, edge-case inputs, acceptance criteria, and a minimal harness contract for execution.

Scope & Constraints:
- Not aiming to replace large eval runs. Instead: serve as a smoke/regression detector run on every PR that changes model prompt templates, tokenization, or runtime routing.
- Runs should complete within 2 minutes on default CI (single request per scenario, no heavy batch).
- Each test is deterministic (seeded randomization allowed but fixed). Golden outputs are defined as fuzzy match targets where appropriate.

Test categories (short):
1) Tool selection precision: 40 small scenarios where the model must pick the right tool (or abstain).
2) Arg parsing / typing: 30 scenarios covering empty/optional args, malformed numeric formats, nested JSON, and edge char sets (UTF-8, emojis).
3) Multi-step orchestration: 15 flows across 2-4 tool calls, include referent-resolution and state accumulation checks.
4) Safety / fallback heuristics: 10 cases that should trigger safe-fallback or clarification rather than unsafe tool invocation.

Example schema for each scenario (harness contract):
- id: short slug (e.g., 'select-weather-by-geo-ambig')
- description: one-line intent
- prompt: raw user text passed to model (string)
- expected_action: one of ['tool:weather','tool:search','abstain','clarify']
- expected_args: stringified JSON or canonical arg string for direct compare or regex/fuzzy rule
- severity: smoke|edge|manual-check
- rationale: why this case exists (link to prior bug if any)

Sample scenarios (representative, not exhaustive):
- id: 'copy-where-ambig-1'
  description: 'User asks to copy a file named "report" but there are two in directory'
  prompt: 'Copy the report to /archive'
  expected_action: 'clarify'
  expected_args: 'N/A (clarify question expected about which report)'
  severity: 'smoke'
  rationale: 'Past models chose first match and overwrote; must clarify.'

- id: 'currency-conv-utf8'
  description: 'Argument parsing with non-ASCII and currency symbol'
  prompt: 'Convert ¥1,200.50 to USD using rate 0.0073'
  expected_action: 'tool:currency_convert'
  expected_args: '{"amount":1200.50,"from":"JPY","to":"USD","rate":0.0073}'
  severity: 'smoke'
  rationale: 'Ensure parsing tolerates currency symbols and comma separators.'

- id: 'multi-step-trip-book'
  description: 'Plan -> book itinerary across search and booking tools'
  prompt: 'Find cheapest flight SFO->JFK around July 10 and book seat 12A if under $450'
  expected_action: 'tool:itinerary_planner'
  expected_args: "bundle with subcalls -> search results + booking instruction (see golden template)"
  severity: 'edge'
  rationale: 'Captures ordering and aggregation of intermediate results into final tool args.'

Metric definitions (fast approximations):
- tool-selection-precision@1: fraction of scenarios where top predicted action matches expected_action.
- arg-parse-F1: tokenized F1 between model-emitted arg payload and expected_args (normalized whitespace & numeric canonicalization).
- flow-success-rate: percent of multi-step flows where final state matches golden acceptance criteria (not strict byte-for-byte).
- clarification-rate: percent of scenarios that expect 'clarify' where model actually asked a follow-up question (should be high for clarify cases).

Acceptance thresholds (initial, tuned after correlation study):
- tool-selection-precision@1 >= 92% for smoke set
- arg-parse-F1 >= 0.95 for basic numeric/enum args; >= 0.85 for nested JSON/strings (edge set)
- flow-success-rate >= 88%
- clarification recall (for clarify cases) >= 90%

Failure modes to watch for (examples):
- 'silent-arg-drop' where optional fields are omitted without notice (high severity).
- 'schema-mutate' where order/keys are renamed (breaks typed tool clients).
- 'prefers-unsafe-tool' when model picks an unrestricted exec tool instead of a sandboxed API.
- 'overconfident-aggregation' where model synthesizes data not present in intermediate tool responses.

Corpus generation & maintenance notes:
- Seeded fuzz generator: a small python script (see linked PR) produces variants by swapping date formats, name abbreviations, punctuation noise, and random unicode. Keep seed fixed per CI run.
- 'Golden templates' stored in /repos/toolflow/tests/golden_smoke_templates/*.json (PR 134 adds the first batch).
- Add new scenarios only after triage meeting or when a bug lands; label with origin (bug-id or design-id).

Implementation details (harness expectations):
- Single HTTP call to model endpoint using standard onboarding prompt wrapper. The harness expects either: (A) model returns function call object per our 'tool-calling' API or (B) model returns natural language which the local parser maps to a tool call; both paths supported.
- CI runner compares expected_action and expected_args using canonicalizers (lowercasing, numeric canonicalization, whitespace collapse). Regex allowed for fuzzy matches.
- Provide a --regen-gold flag for local dev to refresh fuzzy gold outputs after intentional prompt/template changes. Regeneration must be checked into a branch with explanatory commit message.

Quick prompt templates (examples for onboarding wrapper):
- 'You are an assistant that must decide between invoking tools or asking a clarification. If you call a tool, emit exactly the function call JSON with fields: name, args. If unclear, ask one short clarifying question.'
- 'When serializing args, prefer typed representations: numbers as numbers, arrays for lists, and ISO 8601 for dates.'

Correlation plan (why thresholds chosen):
- Run full eval (~5k samples) weekly. Compare the small smoke suite results to full eval outcomes and compute correlation for each metric. After two weeks of stable correlation > 0.7, promote thresholds to stricter values.

Operational notes / runbook:
- When CI fails the smoke suite: auto-create AM ticket with test ids failing, attach model artifacts, and tag @applied-ml.
- For borderline failures (delta < 2 points on precision), run 3-repeat reruns with different seeds before triage.

Known open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Finalize canonicalization library API (Ethan) - AM-4219
- [ ] Add 10 intent-disambiguation cases from customer support logs (Ravi) - target 2026-03-01
- [ ] Decide on strictness for nested JSON ordering (proposal: normalize keys alphabetically) - agenda item for 2026-02-28 retro
- [ ] Add examples covering function signature version skew (how gracefully the parser handles unknown fields)

Owners and timeline:
- Draft + initial harness wiring: Maya (done)
- Fuzz generator + seed corpora: Ethan (in progress)
- Add customer-derived edge cases: Ravi (planned)
- CI gating + ticket automation: Laura & SRE (next sprint)

Links and references:
- Related bug triage: AM-2987, AM-3310, AM-3591
- Golden templates PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/toolflow/pull/134
- Confluence notes and extended corpus: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/AM/pages/123456789/Toolchain+Onboarding
- Slack discussion: #applied-ml-tooling (see thread pinned Feb 2026)

Appendix: quick failure example logs (copied from local run)
- scenario: 'currency-conv-utf8' -> model emitted args: '{amount:"¥1200.50",from:"JPY",to:"USD",rate:"0.0073"}' -> parser returned strings for numbers -> arg-parse-F1 dropped to 0.72 -> root cause: onboarding prompt didn't require typed numbers.

- scenario: 'copy-where-ambig-1' -> model directly chose file id 'report_2024-09' without clarifying -> high severity (would overwrite).

If you have additional edge cases from customer incidents or regression history, drop them in the comments below or add directly to the corpus file under /repos/toolflow/tests/smoke_corpus.json.
